Although there have been widespread rumors that the iPhone 18 Pro will start at US$1,399, this claim may be exaggerated, but a significant price hike for this year's new lineup is almost a foregone conclusion.

Apple has actually been preparing for the pricing shock that will come with the launch of the new models, paving the way with the all-new Apple Upgrade program; now T-Mobile has also responded by rolling out a new 3-year installment plan……

As early as June, Apple had already raised prices significantly across most of its product lines in response to a sharp rise in memory costs. Although existing iPhones have not been affected, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will definitely be more expensive than the previous generation.

The Apple Upgrade lease program can lower users' monthly payments for various products (including the iPhone). However, the biggest catch is that you won't actually own the product after the payment period ends. Many customers may ultimately get trapped in an endless cycle of Apple Upgrade leases.

T-Mobile will launch an all-new installment plan tomorrow, allowing customers to spread the cost of the iPhone and all related fees over 3 years instead of 2. The plan is called EIP Flex 36, and the company says it will attract customers with zero interest and zero down payment.

It's worth noting that both offers come with conditions: zero down payment and zero interest only apply to customers with good credit ratings. The fine print also indicates that some customers' actual annual percentage rate could be as high as 24%. But if you qualify and plan to use your next iPhone for 3 years or more, this deal could be quite attractive.
